results.title: Kow Essuman threatens legal action over unpaid salary arrears, terminal benefits
results.content: Former legal counsel to President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, Kow Essuman, has threatened legal action against the government over unpaid salary arrears and terminal benefits, saying efforts to resolve the matter through correspondence have yielded no response. The dispute follows a letter from his lawyers, Vint & Aletheia, to the Finance Minister, Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, demanding payment of Mr Essuman’s outstanding salary arrears and terminal benefits by Friday, September 11, 2026. The lawyers warned that failure to settle the claims by the deadline could result in legal action. results.title: Uwumborche Gideon seeks to retain Saboba NPP secretary post, pledges stronger organisation
results.content: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) Constituency Secretary for Saboba, Uwumborche Bitermi Gideon, is seeking re-election, pledging to strengthen the party’s grassroots structures, improve internal communication and promote unity ahead of the 2028 general elections. Mr Uwumborche, who has held the position since 2022, says his priority if re-elected will be to ensure that party branches remain active, meetings are properly coordinated and the constituency organisation remains vibrant. He also plans to improve communication between polling stations, electoral areas and the constituency executive, while supporting membership mobilisation and voter outreach across the constituency. “I want to build a constituency that is organised, vibrant and ready to recapture power in Saboba,” he said.

results.title: CJID announces 2026 Excellence in Media Awards finalists across nine West African countries
results.content: The Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID) has announced the finalists for the 2026 Excellence in Media Awards, following submissions from journalists across nine West African countries. The third edition of the awards, which began in 2024, attracted 424 entries from 277 journalists, representing a 54.2 per cent increase on the 275 entries received for the 2025 edition. Submissions came from Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal, The Gambia, Sierra Leone, Côte d’Ivoire, Liberia, Guinea and Benin. The awards recognise journalism that contributes to public accountability, promotes human rights and addresses critical social and development issues across the region. According to CJID, entries first underwent a screening process, after which the top five submissions in each of the eight award categories were presented to an independent panel of judges for assessment.
